schema_version: case_checklist_v1
case_unit_id: SimpleCalendarAddOneEvent
domain: androidworld
task_id: SimpleCalendarAddOneEvent
native:
  user_goal:
    text: Create one Simple Calendar Pro event on the specified date and hour, with the specified title, description, and duration.
    support:
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/single/calendar/calendar.py::SimpleCalendarAddOneEvent.template
  benchmark_success:
    text: Native success requires both runner completion (`interaction_results.done=true`) and a final Simple Calendar `events` table that passes `AddMultipleRows.is_successful` for this case by satisfying `validate_event_addition_integrity` against the initialized noise-only before-state and the single official target event.
    support:
    - official/install/android_world/suite_utils.py::_run_task
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/common_validators/sqlite_validators.py::SQLiteApp.initialize_task
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/common_validators/sqlite_validators.py::AddMultipleRows.initialize_task
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/common_validators/sqlite_validators.py::AddMultipleRows.is_successful
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/single/calendar/calendar.py::SimpleCalendarAddOneEvent.validate_addition_integrity
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/single/calendar/calendar_evaluators.py::validate_event_addition_integrity
  checked_by:
    text: Runner done-gate plus `AddMultipleRows.is_successful`, which reads the final `events` table and applies `validate_event_addition_integrity` for the official added event.
    support:
    - official/install/android_world/suite_utils.py::_run_task
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/common_validators/sqlite_validators.py::AddMultipleRows.is_successful
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/single/calendar/calendar.py::SimpleCalendarAddOneEvent.validate_addition_integrity
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/single/calendar/calendar_evaluators.py::validate_event_addition_integrity
  decisive_artifacts:
  - artifact: Retained final dump/snapshot of Simple Calendar Pro `events` table from `events.db`.
    question: Does the final table retain every initialized noise row unchanged and contain exactly one additional row matching the official target event under the evaluator's comparison on `start_ts`, `end_ts`, `title`, `location`, and `description`, with no other added, removed, or altered rows?
    support:
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/common_validators/sqlite_validators.py::SQLiteApp.initialize_task
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/common_validators/sqlite_validators.py::AddMultipleRows.initialize_task
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/common_validators/sqlite_validators.py::validate_rows_addition_integrity
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/single/calendar/calendar.py::SimpleCalendarAddOneEvent.validate_addition_integrity
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/single/calendar/calendar_evaluators.py::validate_event_addition_integrity
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/single/calendar/calendar_utils.py::EVENTS_TABLE
  - artifact: Retained episode trace or termination record showing whether the run finished with `done=true` or `done=false`.
    question: Did the episode complete with `interaction_results.done=true` rather than ending incomplete?
    support:
    - official/install/android_world/suite_utils.py::_run_task
  success_if:
  - text: Retained completion evidence shows the episode ended with `done=true`.
    support:
    - official/install/android_world/suite_utils.py::_run_task
  - text: The retained final Simple Calendar `events` table shows every initialized noise row still present and exactly one added row matching the official event under the evaluator's comparison on `start_ts`, `end_ts`, `title`, `location`, and `description`, with final row count equal to initial noise rows plus one.
    support:
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/common_validators/sqlite_validators.py::SQLiteApp.initialize_task
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/common_validators/sqlite_validators.py::AddMultipleRows.initialize_task
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/common_validators/sqlite_validators.py::validate_rows_addition_integrity
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/single/calendar/calendar.py::SimpleCalendarAddOneEvent.validate_addition_integrity
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/single/calendar/calendar_evaluators.py::validate_event_addition_integrity
  fail_if:
  - text: Retained completion evidence shows `done=false`; the runner gates the native result to failure even if the database state would otherwise pass.
    support:
    - official/install/android_world/suite_utils.py::_run_task
  - text: The retained final `events` table has no added row matching the official target event under the evaluator's comparison.
    support:
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/common_validators/sqlite_validators.py::AddMultipleRows.is_successful
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/common_validators/sqlite_validators.py::validate_rows_addition_integrity
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/single/calendar/calendar.py::SimpleCalendarAddOneEvent.validate_addition_integrity
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/single/calendar/calendar_evaluators.py::validate_event_addition_integrity
  - text: The retained final `events` table shows wrong final row count or any non-target row removed, altered, or unexpectedly added.
    support:
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/common_validators/sqlite_validators.py::validate_rows_addition_integrity
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/single/calendar/calendar_evaluators.py::validate_event_addition_integrity
  undecided_if:
  - text: Usable retained completion evidence for the runner's `done` gate is missing or indeterminate, and the available underlying table evidence does not independently establish failure.
    support:
    - official/install/android_world/suite_utils.py::_run_task
  - text: A usable retained final `events` table snapshot/dump is missing or unreadable, and retained completion evidence alone does not establish `done=false`.
    support:
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/common_validators/sqlite_validators.py::AddMultipleRows.is_successful
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/single/calendar/calendar_utils.py::DB_PATH
    - official/install/android_world/suite_utils.py::_run_task
stronger:
  additional_conditions:
  - id: exact_title_match
    text: Beyond native success, the added event's `title` exactly equals the official `event_title`; native scoring is weaker because it accepts fuzzy title matches.
    rationale: The task text specifies a concrete title string, but the released validator treats `title` as a free-form field and compares it with fuzzy matching rather than exact equality.
    decisive_artifacts:
    - artifact: Retained final dump/snapshot of Simple Calendar Pro `events` table from `events.db`.
      question: Does the added event's stored `title` exactly equal the official `event_title` string, not just an approximate fuzzy match?
      support:
      - official/install/android_world/task_evals/single/calendar/calendar.py::SimpleCalendarAddOneEvent.template
      - official/install/android_world/task_evals/common_validators/sqlite_validators.py::validate_rows_addition_integrity
      - official/install/android_world/task_evals/single/calendar/calendar_evaluators.py::validate_event_addition_integrity
      - official/install/android_world/utils/fuzzy_match_lib.py::fuzzy_match
      - official/install/android_world/utils/fuzzy_match_lib.py::_MIN_DIFF_SIMILARITY
    support:
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/single/calendar/calendar.py::SimpleCalendarAddOneEvent.template
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/common_validators/sqlite_validators.py::validate_rows_addition_integrity
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/single/calendar/calendar_evaluators.py::validate_event_addition_integrity
    - official/install/android_world/utils/fuzzy_match_lib.py::fuzzy_match
    - official/install/android_world/utils/fuzzy_match_lib.py::_MIN_DIFF_SIMILARITY
  - id: exact_description_match
    text: Beyond native success, the added event's `description` exactly equals the official `event_description`; native scoring is weaker because it accepts fuzzy description matches.
    rationale: The task text specifies a concrete description string, but the released validator treats `description` as a free-form field and compares it with fuzzy matching rather than exact equality.
    decisive_artifacts:
    - artifact: Retained final dump/snapshot of Simple Calendar Pro `events` table from `events.db`.
      question: Does the added event's stored `description` exactly equal the official `event_description` string, not just an approximate fuzzy match?
      support:
      - official/install/android_world/task_evals/single/calendar/calendar.py::SimpleCalendarAddOneEvent.template
      - official/install/android_world/task_evals/common_validators/sqlite_validators.py::validate_rows_addition_integrity
      - official/install/android_world/task_evals/single/calendar/calendar_evaluators.py::validate_event_addition_integrity
      - official/install/android_world/utils/fuzzy_match_lib.py::fuzzy_match
      - official/install/android_world/utils/fuzzy_match_lib.py::_MIN_DIFF_SIMILARITY
    support:
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/single/calendar/calendar.py::SimpleCalendarAddOneEvent.template
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/common_validators/sqlite_validators.py::validate_rows_addition_integrity
    - official/install/android_world/task_evals/single/calendar/calendar_evaluators.py::validate_event_addition_integrity
    - official/install/android_world/utils/fuzzy_match_lib.py::fuzzy_match
    - official/install/android_world/utils/fuzzy_match_lib.py::_MIN_DIFF_SIMILARITY

ways to complete a task, pick the easiest one. Also when something does not work as expected (due to various reasons), sometimes a simple retry can solve the problem, but if it doesn't (you can see that from the history), try to switch to other solutions.\n- Sometimes you may need to navigate the phone to gather information needed to complete the task, for example if user asks \"what is my schedule tomorrow\", then you may want to open the calendar app (using the `open_app` action), look up information there, answer user's question (using the `answer` action) and finish (using the `status` action with complete as goal_status).\n- For requests that are questions (or chat messages), remember to use the `answer` action to reply to user explicitly before finish! follow:\nGeneral\n- Usually there will be multiple ways to complete a task, pick the easiest one. Also when something does not work as expected (due to various reasons), sometimes a simple retry can solve the problem, but if it doesn't (you can see that from the history), try to switch to other solutions.\n- Sometimes you may need to navigate the phone to gather information needed to complete the task, for example if user asks \"what is my schedule tomorrow\", then you may want to open the calendar app (using the `open_app` action), look up information there, answer user's question (using the `answer` action) and finish (using the `status` action with complete as goal_status).\n- For requests that are questions (or chat messages), remember to use the `answer` action to reply to user explicitly before finish! Here are some useful guidelines you need to follow:
General
- Usually there will be multiple ways to complete a task, pick the easiest one. Also when something does not work as expected (due to various reasons), sometimes a simple retry can solve the problem, but if it doesn't (you can see that from the history), try to switch to other solutions.
- Sometimes you may need to navigate the phone to gather information needed to complete the task, for example if user asks "what is my schedule tomorrow", then you may want to open the calendar app (using the `open_app` action), look up information there, answer user's question (using the `answer` action) and finish (using the `status` action with complete as goal_status).
- For requests that are questions (or chat messages), remember to use the `answer` action to reply to user explicitly before finish! Merely displaying the answer on the screen is NOT sufficient (unless the goal is something like "show me ...").
- If the desired state is already achieved (e.g., enabling Wi-Fi when it's already on), you can just complete the task.

General
- Usually there will be multiple ways to complete a task, pick the easiest one. Also when something does not work as expected (due to various reasons), sometimes a simple retry can solve the problem, but if it doesn't (you can see that from the history), try to switch to other solutions.

- For requests that are questions (or chat messages), remember to use the `answer` action to reply to user explicitly before finish! Merely displaying the answer on the screen is NOT sufficient (unless the goal is something like "show me ...").
- If the desired state is already achieved (e.g., enabling Wi-Fi when it's already on), you can just complete the task.
Action Related
- Use the `open_app` action whenever you want to open an app (nothing will happen if the app is not installed), do not use the app drawer to open an app unless all other ways have failed.
- Use the `input_text` action whenever you want to type something (including password) instead of clicking characters on the keyboard one by one. Sometimes there is some default text in the text field you want to type in, remember to delete them before typing.
- For `click`, `long_press` and `input_text`, the index parameter you pick must be VISIBLE in the screenshot and also in the UI element list given to you (some elements in the list may NOT be visible on the screen so you can not interact with them).
- Consider exploring the screen by using the `scroll` action with different directions to reveal additional content.
- The direction parameter for the `scroll` action can be confusing sometimes as it's opposite to swipe, for example, to view content at the bottom, the `scroll` direction should be set to "down". Usually the text selected from the previous step is NOT the one you want, you need to adjust the range by dragging the two pointers. If you want to select all text in the text field, simply click the `select all` button in the bar.

- To delete some text: the most traditional way is to place the cursor at the right place and use the backspace button in the keyboard to delete the characters one by one (can long press the backspace to accelerate if there are many to delete). Another approach is to first select the text you want to delete, then click the backspace button in the keyboard.
- To copy some text: first select the exact text you want to copy, which usually also brings up the text selection bar, then click the `copy` button in bar.
- To paste text into a text box, first long press the text box, then usually the text selection bar will appear with a `paste` button in it.

General
- Usually there will be multiple ways to complete a task, pick the easiest one. Also when something does not work as expected (due to various reasons), sometimes a simple retry can solve the problem, but if it doesn't (you can see that from the history), try to switch to other solutions.
- Sometimes you may need to navigate the phone to gather information needed to complete the task, for example if user asks "what is my schedule tomorrow", then you may want to open the calendar app (using the `open_app` action), look up information there, answer user's question (using the `answer` action) and finish (using the `status` action with complete as goal_status).
- For requests that are questions (or chat messages), remember to use the `answer` action to reply to user explicitly before finish! Merely displaying the answer on the screen is NOT sufficient (unless the goal is something like "show me ...").
- If the desired state is already achieved (e.g., enabling Wi-Fi when it's already on), you can just complete the task.
Action Related
- Use the `open_app` action whenever you want to open an app (nothing will happen if the app is not installed), do not use the app drawer to open an app unless all other ways have failed.
- Use the `input_text` action whenever you want to type something (including password) instead of clicking characters on the keyboard one by one. Sometimes there is some default text in the text field you want to type in, remember to delete them before typing.
- For `click`, `long_press` and `input_text`, the index parameter you pick must be VISIBLE in the screenshot and also in the UI element list given to you (some elements in the list may NOT be visible on the screen so you can not interact with them).
- Consider exploring the screen by using the `scroll` action with different directions to reveal additional content.
- The direction parameter for the `scroll` action can be confusing sometimes as it's opposite to swipe, for example, to view content at the bottom, the `scroll` direction should be set to "down". Text Related Operations
- Normally to select some text on the screen: <i> Enter text selection mode by long pressing the area where the text is, then some of the words near the long press point will be selected (highlighted with two pointers indicating the range) and usually a text selection bar will also appear with options like `copy`, `paste`, `select all`, etc. <ii> Select the exact text you need. Usually the text selected from the previous step is NOT the one you want, you need to adjust the range by dragging the two pointers. If you want to select all text in the text field, simply click the `select all` button in the bar.
- At this point, you don't have the ability to drag something around the screen, so in general you can not select arbitrary text.
- To delete some text: the most traditional way is to place the cursor at the right place and use the backspace button in the keyboard to delete the characters one by one (can long press the backspace to accelerate if there are many to delete). Another approach is to first select the text you want to delete, then click the backspace button in the keyboard.
- To copy some text: first select the exact text you want to copy, which usually also brings up the text selection bar, then click the `copy` button in bar.
- To paste text into a text box, first long press the text box, then usually the text selection bar will appear with a `paste` button in it.
- When typing into a text field, sometimes an auto-complete dropdown list will appear. This usually indicating this is a enum field and you should try to select the best match by clicking the corresponding one in the list.

Here are some useful guidelines you need to follow:
General
- Usually there will be multiple ways to complete a task, pick the easiest one. Also when something does not work as expected (due to various reasons), sometimes a simple retry can solve the problem, but if it doesn't (you can see that from the history), try to switch to other solutions.
- Sometimes you may need to navigate the phone to gather information needed to complete the task, for example if user asks "what is my schedule tomorrow", then you may want to open the calendar app (using the `open_app` action), look up information there, answer user's question (using the `answer` action) and finish (using the `status` action with complete as goal_status).
- For requests that are questions (or chat messages), remember to use the `answer` action to reply to user explicitly before finish! Merely displaying the answer on the screen is NOT sufficient (unless the goal is something like "show me ...").
- If the desired state is already achieved (e.g., enabling Wi-Fi when it's already on), you can just complete the task.
Action Related
- Use the `open_app` action whenever you want to open an app (nothing will happen if the app is not installed), do not use the app drawer to open an app unless all other ways have failed.
- Use the `input_text` action whenever you want to type something (including password) instead of clicking characters on the keyboard one by one. Sometimes there is some default text in the text field you want to type in, remember to delete them before typing.
- For `click`, `long_press` and `input_text`, the index parameter you pick must be VISIBLE in the screenshot and also in the UI element list given to you (some elements in the list may NOT be visible on the screen so you can not interact with them).
- Consider exploring the screen by using the `scroll` action with different directions to reveal additional content.
- The direction parameter for the `scroll` action can be confusing sometimes as it's opposite to swipe, for example, to view content at the bottom, the `scroll` direction should be set to "down". It has been observed that you have difficulties in choosing the correct direction, so if one does not work, try the opposite as well.
Text Related Operations
- Normally to select some text on the screen: <i> Enter text selection mode by long pressing the area where the text is, then some of the words near the long press point will be selected (highlighted with two pointers indicating the range) and usually a text selection bar will also appear with options like `copy`, `paste`, `select all`, etc. <ii> Select the exact text you need. Usually the text selected from the previous step is NOT the one you want, you need to adjust the range by dragging the two pointers. If you want to select all text in the text field, simply click the `select all` button in the bar.
- At this point, you don't have the ability to drag something around the screen, so in general you can not select arbitrary text.

Here are some useful guidelines you need to follow:
General
- Usually there will be multiple ways to complete a task, pick the easiest one. Also when something does not work as expected (due to various reasons), sometimes a simple retry can solve the problem, but if it doesn't (you can see that from the history), try to switch to other solutions.
- Sometimes you may need to navigate the phone to gather information needed to complete the task, for example if user asks "what is my schedule tomorrow", then you may want to open the calendar app (using the `open_app` action), look up information there, answer user's question (using the `answer` action) and finish (using the `status` action with complete as goal_status).
- For requests that are questions (or chat messages), remember to use the `answer` action to reply to user explicitly before finish! Merely displaying the answer on the screen is NOT sufficient (unless the goal is something like "show me ...").
- If the desired state is already achieved (e.g., enabling Wi-Fi when it's already on), you can just complete the task.
Action Related
- Use the `open_app` action whenever you want to open an app (nothing will happen if the app is not installed), do not use the app drawer to open an app unless all other ways have failed.
- Use the `input_text` action whenever you want to type something (including password) instead of clicking characters on the keyboard one by one. Sometimes there is some default text in the text field you want to type in, remember to delete them before typing.
- For `click`, `long_press` and `input_text`, the index parameter you pick must be VISIBLE in the screenshot and also in the UI element list given to you (some elements in the list may NOT be visible on the screen so you can not interact with them).
- Consider exploring the screen by using the `scroll` action with different directions to reveal additional content.
- The direction parameter for the `scroll` action can be confusing sometimes as it's opposite to swipe, for example, to view content at the bottom, the `scroll` direction should be set to "down". It has been observed that you have difficulties in choosing the correct direction, so if one does not work, try the opposite as well.
Text Related Operations
- Normally to select some text on the screen: <i> Enter text selection mode by long pressing the area where the text is, then some of the words near the long press point will be selected (highlighted with two pointers indicating the range) and usually a text selection bar will also appear with options like `copy`, `paste`, `select all`, etc. <ii> Select the exact text you need. Usually the text selected from the previous step is NOT the one you want, you need to adjust the range by dragging the two pointers. Here are some useful guidelines you need to follow:
General
- Usually there will be multiple ways to complete a task, pick the easiest one. Also when something does not work as expected (due to various reasons), sometimes a simple retry can solve the problem, but if it doesn't (you can see that from the history), try to switch to other solutions.
- Sometimes you may need to navigate the phone to gather information needed to complete the task, for example if user asks "what is my schedule tomorrow", then you may want to open the calendar app (using the `open_app` action), look up information there, answer user's question (using the `answer` action) and finish (using the `status` action with complete as goal_status).
- For requests that are questions (or chat messages), remember to use the `answer` action to reply to user explicitly before finish! Merely displaying the answer on the screen is NOT sufficient (unless the goal is something like "show me ...").
- If the desired state is already achieved (e.g., enabling Wi-Fi when it's already on), you can just complete the task.
Action Related
- Use the `open_app` action whenever you want to open an app (nothing will happen if the app is not installed), do not use the app drawer to open an app unless all other ways have failed.
- Use the `input_text` action whenever you want to type something (including password) instead of clicking characters on the keyboard one by one. Sometimes there is some default text in the text field you want to type in, remember to delete them before typing.
- For `click`, `long_press` and `input_text`, the index parameter you pick must be VISIBLE in the screenshot and also in the UI element list given to you (some elements in the list may NOT be visible on the screen so you can not interact with them).
- Consider exploring the screen by using the `scroll` action with different directions to reveal additional content.
- The direction parameter for the `scroll` action can be confusing sometimes as it's opposite to swipe, for example, to view content at the bottom, the `scroll` direction should be set to "down". Text Related Operations

Usually the text selected from the previous step is NOT the one you want, you need to adjust the range by dragging the two pointers. If you want to select all text in the text field, simply click the `select all` button in the bar.

Another approach is to first select the text you want to delete, then click the backspace button in the keyboard.
- To copy some text: first select the exact text you want to copy, which usually also brings up the text selection bar, then click the `copy` button in bar.
- To paste text into a text box, first long press the text box, then usually the text selection bar will appear with a `paste` button in it.

- If the desired state is already achieved (e.g., enabling Wi-Fi when it's already on), you can just complete the task.

General
- Usually there will be multiple ways to complete a task, pick the easiest one. Also when something does not work as expected (due to various reasons), sometimes a simple retry can solve the problem, but if it doesn't (you can see that from the history), try to switch to other solutions.
- Sometimes you may need to navigate the phone to gather information needed to complete the task, for example if user asks "what is my schedule tomorrow", then you may want to open the calendar app (using the `open_app` action), look up information there, answer user's question (using the `answer` action) and finish (using the `status` action with complete as goal_status).
- For requests that are questions (or chat messages), remember to use the `answer` action to reply to user explicitly before finish! Merely displaying the answer on the screen is NOT sufficient (unless the goal is something like "show me ...").
- If the desired state is already achieved (e.g., enabling Wi-Fi when it's already on), you can just complete the task.
Action Related
- Use the `open_app` action whenever you want to open an app (nothing will happen if the app is not installed), do not use the app drawer to open an app unless all other ways have failed.
- Use the `input_text` action whenever you want to type something (including password) instead of clicking characters on the keyboard one by one. Sometimes there is some default text in the text field you want to type in, remember to delete them before typing.
- For `click`, `long_press` and `input_text`, the index parameter you pick must be VISIBLE in the screenshot and also in the UI element list given to you (some elements in the list may NOT be visible on the screen so you can not interact with them).
- Consider exploring the screen by using the `scroll` action with different directions to reveal additional content.

Text Related Operations
- Normally to select some text on the screen: <i> Enter text selection mode by long pressing the area where the text is, then some of the words near the long press point will be selected (highlighted with two pointers indicating the range) and usually a text selection bar will also appear with options like `copy`, `paste`, `select all`, etc. <ii> Select the exact text you need. Usually the text selected from the previous step is NOT the one you want, you need to adjust the range by dragging the two pointers. If you want to select all text in the text field, simply click the `select all` button in the bar.

Another approach is to first select the text you want to delete, then click the backspace button in the keyboard.
- To copy some text: first select the exact text you want to copy, which usually also brings up the text selection bar, then click the `copy` button in bar.
- To paste text into a text box, first long press the text box, then usually the text selection bar will appear with a `paste` button in it.

Here are some useful guidelines you need to follow:
General
- Usually there will be multiple ways to complete a task, pick the easiest one. Also when something does not work as expected (due to various reasons), sometimes a simple retry can solve the problem, but if it doesn't (you can see that from the history), try to switch to other solutions.
- Sometimes you may need to navigate the phone to gather information needed to complete the task, for example if user asks "what is my schedule tomorrow", then you may want to open the calendar app (using the `open_app` action), look up information there, answer user's question (using the `answer` action) and finish (using the `status` action with complete as goal_status).
- For requests that are questions (or chat messages), remember to use the `answer` action to reply to user explicitly before finish! Merely displaying the answer on the screen is NOT sufficient (unless the goal is something like "show me ...").
- If the desired state is already achieved (e.g., enabling Wi-Fi when it's already on), you can just complete the task.
Action Related
- Use the `open_app` action whenever you want to open an app (nothing will happen if the app is not installed), do not use the app drawer to open an app unless all other ways have failed.
- Use the `input_text` action whenever you want to type something (including password) instead of clicking characters on the keyboard one by one. Sometimes there is some default text in the text field you want to type in, remember to delete them before typing.
- For `click`, `long_press` and `input_text`, the index parameter you pick must be VISIBLE in the screenshot and also in the UI element list given to you (some elements in the list may NOT be visible on the screen so you can not interact with them).
- Consider exploring the screen by using the `scroll` action with different directions to reveal additional content.
- The direction parameter for the `scroll` action can be confusing sometimes as it's opposite to swipe, for example, to view content at the bottom, the `scroll` direction should be set to "down". It has been observed that you have difficulties in choosing the correct direction, so if one does not work, try the opposite as well.
Text Related Operations
- Normally to select some text on the screen: <i> Enter text selection mode by long pressing the area where the text is, then some of the words near the long press point will be selected (highlighted with two pointers indicating the range) and usually a text selection bar will also appear with options like `copy`, `paste`, `select all`, etc. <ii> Select the exact text you need. Usually the text selected from the previous step is NOT the one you want, you need to adjust the range by dragging the two pointers. If you want to select all text in the text field, simply click the `select all` button in the bar.
- At this point, you don't have the ability to drag something around the screen, so in general you can not select arbitrary text.
- To delete some text: the most traditional way is to place the cursor at the right place and use the backspace button in the keyboard to delete the characters one by one (can long press the backspace to accelerate if there are many to delete). Another approach is to first select the text you want to delete, then click the backspace button in the keyboard.
- To copy some text: first select the exact text you want to copy, which usually also brings up the text selection bar, then click the `copy` button in bar.
- To paste text into a text box, first long press the text box, then usually the text selection bar will appear with a `paste` button in it.
- When typing into a text field, sometimes an auto-complete dropdown list will appear. This usually indicating this is a enum field and you should try to select the best match by clicking the corresponding one in the list.

Here are some useful guidelines you need to follow:
General
- Usually there will be multiple ways to complete a task, pick the easiest one. Also when something does not work as expected (due to various reasons), sometimes a simple retry can solve the problem, but if it doesn't (you can see that from the history), try to switch to other solutions.
- Sometimes you may need to navigate the phone to gather information needed to complete the task, for example if user asks "what is my schedule tomorrow", then you may want to open the calendar app (using the `open_app` action), look up information there, answer user's question (using the `answer` action) and finish (using the `status` action with complete as goal_status).
- For requests that are questions (or chat messages), remember to use the `answer` action to reply to user explicitly before finish! Merely displaying the answer on the screen is NOT sufficient (unless the goal is something like "show me ...").
- If the desired state is already achieved (e.g., enabling Wi-Fi when it's already on), you can just complete the task.
Action Related
- Use the `open_app` action whenever you want to open an app (nothing will happen if the app is not installed), do not use the app drawer to open an app unless all other ways have failed.
- Use the `input_text` action whenever you want to type something (including password) instead of clicking characters on the keyboard one by one. Sometimes there is some default text in the text field you want to type in, remember to delete them before typing.
- For `click`, `long_press` and `input_text`, the index parameter you pick must be VISIBLE in the screenshot and also in the UI element list given to you (some elements in the list may NOT be visible on the screen so you can not interact with them).
- Consider exploring the screen by using the `scroll` action with different directions to reveal additional content.
- The direction parameter for the `scroll` action can be confusing sometimes as it's opposite to swipe, for example, to view content at the bottom, the `scroll` direction should be set to "down". It has been observed that you have difficulties in choosing the correct direction, so if one does not work, try the opposite as well.
Text Related Operations
- Normally to select some text on the screen: <i> Enter text selection mode by long pressing the area where the text is, then some of the words near the long press point will be selected (highlighted with two pointers indicating the range) and usually a text selection bar will also appear with options like `copy`, `paste`, `select all`, etc. <ii> Select the exact text you need. Usually the text selected from the previous step is NOT the one you want, you need to adjust the range by dragging the two pointers. If you want to select all text in the text field, simply click the `select all` button in the bar.
- At this point, you don't have the ability to drag something around the screen, so in general you can not select arbitrary text.
- To delete some text: the most traditional way is to place the cursor at the right place and use the backspace button in the keyboard to delete the characters one by one (can long press the backspace to accelerate if there are many to delete). Another approach is to first select the text you want to delete, then click the backspace button in the keyboard.
- To copy some text: first select the exact text you want to copy, which usually also brings up the text selection bar, then click the `copy` button in bar.
- To paste text into a text box, first long press the text box, then usually the text selection bar will appear with a `paste` button in it.
- When typing into a text field, sometimes an auto-complete dropdown list will appear. This usually indicating this is a enum field and you should try to select the best match by clicking the corresponding one in the list.
